record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: parameterized complexity for hard social-network exchange cases
record.original_question: For the NP-hard cases of deciding reachability of a matching and finding a Pareto-optimal reachable matching in house allocation via swaps on a social network, what fixed-parameter or other parameterized algorithms are possible?

evidence.quote: Also, the hard cases in Theorems 5 and 6 could be tackled from a parameterised complexity viewpoint.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following house allocation model on a social network. Let G=(V,E) be an undirected graph whose vertices V={1,...,n} are agents, and let H be a set of n indivisible objects ("houses"). Each agent i has a strict linear preference order ≻_i over H. An allocation (matching) is a bijection μ : V → H. Given an initial allocation μ_0, a swap is the exchange of the houses currently held by two agents i,j that are adjacent in G (i.e., {i,j}∈E); the swap is called rational (or Pareto-improving) if μ(i)≻_i μ(j) implies the swapped result strictly improves at least one of i,j and does not make the other worse off (and is rational for both). An allocation μ is reachable from μ_0 if there is a finite sequence of such rational swaps transforming μ_0 into μ. An allocation μ is Pareto-optimal if no other allocation gives every agent a weakly better house and at least one agent a strictly better house.

Two decision problems are known to be NP-hard in this framework:
(i) Reachable Matching: given (G, ≻, μ_0, μ), decide whether μ is reachable from μ_0;
(ii) Pareto-Optimal Reachable Matching: given (G, ≻, μ_0), decide whether there exists a Pareto-optimal allocation reachable from μ_0 (equivalently, find one if it exists).

Problem. For each of these NP-hard problems, design fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms, or otherwise classify their parameterized complexity (FPT, W[1]-hard, XP, para-NP-hard, etc.), with respect to natural parameters such as the number of agents whose endowment changes, the number of distinct preference profiles, the treewidth, vertex cover number, or maximum degree of G, the number of houses preferred by each agent over their initial endowment, or combinations thereof.
artifact.category_tag: Parameterized complexity of matching under preferences
artifact.status_search_result: There has been follow-up work on the parameterized complexity of Reachable Object / Reachable Matching via swaps on social networks (e.g., investigations on trees, stars, and cliques, and on maximum-votes Pareto-efficient allocations via swaps). Several FPT and hardness results have been obtained for specific parameters and graph classes, but a complete parameterized-complexity classification of the NP-hard cases of Reachable Matching and Pareto-Optimal Reachable Matching under all natural parameters does not appear to be settled.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Votes Pareto-Efficient Allocations via Swaps on a Social Network
status_evidence.snippet: Studies computational complexity of reaching Pareto-efficient matchings via swaps along a social network, including hardness and algorithmic results.
status_evidence.claim: Recent follow-up addresses complexity of Pareto-efficient reachable matchings via swaps.

status_evidence.title: Good Things Come to Those Who Swap Objects on Paths
status_evidence.snippet: Provides polynomial-time algorithms for Reachable Object on paths and NP-hardness on trees/cliques.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes hardness boundaries that motivate parameterized study of the NP-hard cases.

status_evidence.title: Object Allocation via Swaps along a Social Network
status_evidence.snippet: Original model by Gourvès, Lesca, Wilczynski introducing reachable object/matching via swaps on social networks.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the framework in which the open parameterized-complexity question is posed.
